chunks: Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: If a person performing tayammum enters into the salat and then experiences that which invalidates wudu (ablution) unintentionally, and he finds water, then he must purify himself and continue from what has already passed of his salat, so long as he has not turned away from the salat so as to face away from it, nor spoken deliberately with words that are not part of the salat. This is indicated by that.
And it was narrated by Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Luʾluʾi, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashir, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAsim: the like of it.

key_terms.مُتَيَمِّمًا: a person in the state of tayammum
key_terms.يَبْنِيَ: to continue or build upon what has preceded
key_terms.ٱسْتِدْبَارِهَا: turning one’s back to it, i.e. facing away from the salat

ai.seo_question: What should a person who prayed with tayammum do if his wudu (ablution) is invalidated and he then finds water during salat?
ai.summary: This text gives a legal ruling regarding one who began salat with tayammum and then unintentionally experienced a state that invalidates wudu (ablution) before finding water. It states that such a person should purify himself and resume the salat from where he left off, provided he has not invalidated the prayer by turning away from it or speaking deliberately outside of it.
